title: Validation of the unary prefix
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle $\mathcal O$, $r$ a register, $p\in\mathbb Z$, and $c$ a configuration on input $x$. Suppose the transition identities $hU0,hU1,hS$ hold at states $vU0,vU1,vS$, respectively, and none of these states is an oracle-call state, as asserted by $cU0,cU1,cS$. If the length of the initial run of ones in $x$ is even and the next two bits are $01$, then the run from state $vU0$ at input-head position $1$ and register-head position $p$ reaches state $vX$ at input-head position $3+tRun(x)$, a valid position. If this bit-pattern condition fails, the run from the same starting configuration halts with a rejecting output. The runs avoid oracle-call states before their endpoint.
hypotheses_covered: Transition identities hU0, hU1, and hS
